interest: U.S. intelligence on the Japanese Navy, from carriers to the Yamato class.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.30 (covering August 1940 through August 1944, with retrospective reports from late 1939) documents U.S. diplomatic, naval, military, and domestic intelligence monitoring of the Imperial Japanese Navy before and during World War II. The collection encompasses Japanese Imperial General Headquarters communiqués detailing naval, air, and riverine operations during the Second Sino-Japanese War; policy analyses of naval deterrence by Stanley K. Hornbeck and Walter Lippmann; pre-hostilities intelligence on secret naval reservist mobilizations, auxiliary merchant conversions, and German engineering collaboration in Chinese ports; covert aircraft carrier conversions and West Coast tanker movements; critical sightings on December 6, 1941, of Japanese invasion convoys bound for Southeast Asia; wartime estimates of Japanese shipbuilding potential and Yamato-class super-battleships gathered from diplomatic contacts in neutral capitals; and intelligence on major high command reorganizations through the fall of the Tojo cabinet in August 1944.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of and intelligence commentary on the Japanese Imperial General Headquarters communique covering 1939 naval operations in China.
subfiles.from: Major William Mayer, Military Attaché
subfiles.summary: Major Mayer forwards a Japanese communiqué on 1939 naval operations in China, with comments on its claims.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report on Japanese Communiqué of 1939 Naval Operations in China

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum analyzing Walter Lippmann's commentary on American sea power and deterrence against Japan in the Pacific.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Political Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck notes Lippmann's column arguing that a Japanese Navy tied down in Asia cannot threaten the Americas.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck on Walter Lippmann's Column on Sea Power

subfiles.about: Consular telegram and State Department paraphrase reporting International Settlement police intelligence regarding a secret mobilization of Japanese naval reservists in China.
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, American Consul General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reports a secret Tokyo order mobilizing Japanese naval reservists in China, November 1940.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1311 from Lockhart (Shanghai) on Mobilization of Japanese Naval Reservists, with Paraphrase

subfiles.about: Record of conversation between Stanley K. Hornbeck and British Charge d'Affaires Butler regarding Japanese naval movements and cautious posture in home waters.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Political Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck records British word that the Japanese Navy urged moderation and kept ships at home.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Stanley K. Hornbeck and Nevile M. Butler on Japanese Naval Posture
subfiles.to: Secretary of State / Under Secretary Sumner Welles

subfiles.about: Consular report, with transmission copies and paraphrase, detailing the reconditioning and armament of captured Chinese vessels at Tsingtao under German supervision as potential raiders.
subfiles.from: Paul W. Meyer, American Consul, Tsingtao
subfiles.summary: Consul Paul W. Meyer reports on the salvage, reconditioning, and arming of three former Chinese ships at Tsingtao: the former naval gunboat Chenhai and merchant steamers Yungsiang and Haili. The Chenhai and Yungsiang have been reconditioned and manned by Japanese naval crews, while the 10,000-ton Haili is being completed in drydock, with intelligence suggesting they may serve as commerce raiders. Meyer identifies two German technicians, W. Wicke and H. Haerting, directing the work, alongside three German companions who departed for Tientsin; he requests that the information be forwarded to American naval authorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7 from Meyer (Tsingtao) on Reconditioning of Chinese Vessels and German Technicians, with Paraphrase

subfiles.about: FBI intelligence letter providing detailed data on Japanese passenger liner construction, oil tankers, naval base construction on the Sea of Japan, and aircraft arsenal output.
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports on Japanese shipbuilding and naval arsenals, including convertible liners at Nagasaki.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr., on Japanese Shipbuilding and Naval Arsenals
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting the unexpected departure for Japan of approximately two-thirds of the Japanese naval officers assigned to the Manchukuo Sungari River flotilla.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Gourley, American Consul, Harbin
subfiles.summary: Gourley reports two-thirds of Japanese officers of the Sungari flotilla suddenly left for Japan, February 1941.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 55 from Gourley (Harbin) on Recall of Japanese Naval Officers from Sungari Flotilla, with Enclosure
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (and Nelson T. Johnson, Peiping)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram and naval liaison teletype relaying a consular report from Nagasaki on the conversion of the liner Kasuga Maru into an aircraft carrier.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew relays Tower's report that the liner Kasuga Maru was being converted to an aircraft carrier.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 576 from Grew (Tokyo) on Conversion of Kasuga Maru to Aircraft Carrier, with OPNAV Teletype
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (relayed to Chief of Naval Operations)

subfiles.about: Biographical intelligence memorandum identifying Vice Admiral Naokuni Nomura as Chief of the Japanese Naval Mission in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Schuler identifies Vice Admiral Naokuni Nomura, head of the naval mission in Berlin.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Schuler (FE) regarding Vice Admiral Naokuni Nomura in Berlin
subfiles.to: H. R. Hill, Department of State

subfiles.about: Informational memorandum and vessel movement schedules documenting the command structure and California port calls of Japanese Naval Special Transports.
subfiles.from: Division of Protocol, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Memo on Japanese Naval Special Transports, with tanker visits to U.S. West Coast ports in 1941.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Schedules on Japanese Naval Special Transports and Pacific Port Movements

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting an imperial ordinance authorizing retired naval special service and noncommissioned officers to return to active duty.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports an ordinance letting retired naval officers rejoin the reserve, August 1941.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1157 from Grew (Tokyo) on Reinstatement of Retired Naval Officers

subfiles.about: Consular telegram and garbled transmission copy describing intense warship refitting, torpedo boat maneuvers, and security at Port Arthur naval base.
subfiles.from: Paul H. Richardson, American Representative / Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Richardson reports intense activity at Port Arthur naval base, October 1941.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Richardson (Dairen) on Naval Activity and Maneuvers at Port Arthur, with Garbled Copy

subfiles.about: Military intelligence report outlining travel options across the Americas considered by the Japanese Naval Mission returning from Axis Europe.
subfiles.from: Office of the Assistant Chief of Staff for Military Intelligence, Headquarters Panama Canal Department
subfiles.summary: Canal Zone report: Japanese naval mission seeking a new route home after the German-Soviet war.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report from Panama Canal Department on Return Route of Japanese Naval Mission
subfiles.to: Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, War Department

subfiles.about: Secret Navy Department memorandum transmitting Asiatic Fleet sighting reports of Japanese troop convoys steaming toward Malaya on December 6, 1941.
subfiles.from: Captain R. E. Schuirmann (by direction, Office of the Chief of Naval Operations)
subfiles.summary: Hart reports Japanese invasion convoys off Indochina on December 6, 1941.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Chief of Naval Operations on Japanese Invasion Convoys Sighted S.W. of Indochina

subfiles.about: FBI intelligence report presenting conflicting estimates by diplomatic internees at White Sulphur Springs regarding Japanese shipbuilding capabilities.
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports interned Japanese claims of three million tons of shipbuilding, disputed by another internee.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr., on Japanese Shipbuilding Capacity Estimates
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: State Department cross-reference sheet indexing intelligence correspondence regarding naval warship models constructed by Swedish Embassy staff.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on Swedish Embassy staff building warship models.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Naval Ship Models Built by Swedish Embassy Personnel
subfiles.to: Federal Bureau of Investigation (J. Edgar Hoover)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram and paraphrase relaying admissions by the Japanese Ambassador to Turkey concerning undisclosed aircraft carrier strength and treaty evasion.
subfiles.from: Laurence A. Steinhardt, American Ambassador to Turkey
subfiles.summary: Steinhardt reports Japan had 14 carriers on December 7, 1941 and kept treaty ships ready.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 35 from Steinhardt (Ankara) on Japanese Carrier Strength and Treaty Evasion, with Paraphrase

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram chain conveying Turkish intelligence on four massive battleships under construction in Japan, confirmed by U.S. military intelligence in China.
subfiles.from: Laurence A. Steinhardt (Ankara) / Cordell Hull (Washington) / Clarence E. Gauss (Chungking)
subfiles.summary: Steinhardt, Hull and Gauss exchange reports of Japan's new 45,000-ton battleships, early news of the Yamato class.
subfiles.title: Telegram Chain on Japanese Construction of Giant Battleships (Yamato Class)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State / American Embassy, Chungking

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram reporting German military press commentary on major high command reassignments within the Imperial Japanese Navy.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, American Minister to Switzerland, Bern
subfiles.summary: Harrison relays German reports of Japan's naval command changes of December 1943.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7623 from Harrison (Bern) on Japanese High Naval Command Reshuffle

subfiles.about: Diplomatic telegram relaying Soviet press reports on the replacement of Admiral Shimada by Admiral Oikawa and naval shifts after the Tojo cabinet's fall.
subfiles.from: W. Averell Harriman, American Ambassador to the Soviet Union, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Harriman reports naval appointments after Tojo's fall, including Oikawa as Chief of the Naval General Staff.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2846 from Harriman (Moscow) on Naval Command Reorganization Following Tojo Resignation
